thread:
incident-bot: Pager — metering: late-emit anomaly detected in eu1. Metric: `usage-emitter.out_of_order_count` spike + overage flags. Possible consumer lag. Severity: P2. @maya on-call.

maya: pulling up dashboards now. seeing a sharp tail in emitter-lag around 12:02 UTC.

jordan: confirmed — consumer group `metering-consumer-eu1` lag ~360k, leader broker i-0a9 stalled. offsets not progressing since 12:01 UTC.

maya: any deploys or config changes in the last hour?

jordan: nothing in deploy history. system noticed GC spikes on emitter pods at ~12:00, then consumer fell behind. kube node eu1-n3 shows OOMKilled on emitter-aggregator-2 at 12:03. attaching quick logs:
```
2026-03-20T12:02:59Z emitter-aggregator-2 OOMKilled java.lang.OutOfMemoryError
2026-03-20T12:03:05Z metering-consumer-eu1 offset commit failed: TimeoutException
2026-03-20T12:03:10Z consumer-lag: +362124
```

billing-ops: FYI — downstream billing saw a surge in overage flag emits starting 12:04 UTC. Customers might receive provisional overage alerts for the 12:00–12:10 window.

samir: I can pause overage notifications in the alerting pipeline for eu1 while we investigate. recommended?

maya: do it. put a 30m mute on `billing-overage-notify.eu1`. annotate in incident timeline.

oncall-bot: Action taken: muted `billing-overage-notify.eu1` for 30m by samir.

jordan: I'm going to restart emitter-aggregator-2 and recycle the consumer group. plan: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/emitter-aggregator -n metering --selector=pod=emitter-aggregator-2` then `kafka-consumer-groups --reset-offsets` if needed. running restart now.

jordan: restart completed, pod came back up at 12:07. consumer started catching up, lag down to 48k at 12:12.

maya: good. Samir, start a dry-run backfill/recon to detect duplicate counts before unmuting. Use recon script and check delta.

samir: running recon (dry-run): `python scripts/recon/usage_repair.py --start 2026-03-20T12:00Z --end 2026-03-20T12:45Z --mode dry-run --consumer-group metering-consumer-eu1`

samir: dry-run shows ~1.2% duplication risk for tokens in that window; suggested remediation: incremental backfill with dedupe, and mark affected accounts for manual review if threshold exceeded.

billing-ops: can we suppress billing-charge calculation for the window until recon completes? We should avoid auto-charging customers on possibly duplicated tokens.

maya: yes — flip billing-calculation to read-only for commit window. samir, coordinate with billing-ops to hold final invoice writes.

samir: setting ledger-write-lock for 12:00-12:45 window -> locked.

laura: drafting a short status page notice: "We're investigating delayed usage reports and potential duplicate overage alerts in EU region (12:00–12:45 UTC). Notifications temporarily paused. We'll update within 60 minutes." I'll post once we confirm backfill plan.

billing-ops: running quick query to enumerate customers with >5% delta in provisional counts: `SELECT cust_id, delta_pct FROM usage_shadow WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-03-20T12:00Z' AND '2026-03-20T12:45Z' ORDER BY delta_pct DESC LIMIT 50;`

jordan: consumer fully caught up at 12:34, lag 0. No further OOMs on pods. kafka broker i-0a9 CPU spike resolved after node drained (k8s preempt).

samir: recon incremental backfill (safe-mode) started at 12:40, estimate 18m. will dedupe and emit reconciliation events to `billing-audit` topic.

maya: OK — timeline: mute in place, restart done, ledger locked, backfill running. If backfill confirms duplicates above threshold we'll rollback provisional overages and trigger manual notices. Keep updates here.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=investigating -> mitigation_in_progress. Next update expected by 12:58 UTC or after backfill completes.
